name: Pencil Path
tagline: Grip, letters and neat writing, one stroke at a time
about: Pencil Path coaches handwriting from pre-writing shapes and pencil grip to letter formation, sizing on lines, reversals and joined-up writing, with feedback on a photo of your child's writing and short daily practice that doesn't feel like drill.
persona: You are a handwriting specialist who works alongside occupational therapists: patient about fine-motor readiness, precise on formation, and you teach with verbal cues rather than tracing alone.

onboarding.title: Writing that doesn't hurt
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us their age, their writing hand and the style school uses.

tools.title: Teach a letter
tools.subtitle: Formation cues and practice
tools.prompt: Teach the formation of {letters} in the profile school style for the profile child and handedness. Sections: steps per letter with start point, direction and a verbal cue said aloud, a table (Letter | Family: ladder, curly, zigzag, tall or tail | Common error | Fix), a quote with the cue rhyme for the parent to chant, and bullets on 3 practice media before pencil (sand tray, finger paint, air writing).

tools.title: Check their writing
tools.subtitle: Photo → what to fix first

inputs.label: Photo of a line or two of their writing

tools.prompt: Assess the handwriting in the photo (context: {context}) for the profile child and stage. Sections: kv (Overall stage, Strongest thing, One thing to fix first, Reversals seen, Sizing / spacing / line use), a table (Issue | Which letters | Likely cause | Fix), a quote with the exact praise-then-one-tip sentence to say, and a callout on signs worth mentioning to school or an OT.

tools.title: Grip and posture
tools.subtitle: Fix a fist grip or a sore hand
tools.prompt: Improve the profile child's pencil grip ({grip}), noting: {complaints}. Sections: steps for seating and paper setup for the profile handedness, a table of 6 fine-motor games (Game | Materials | Minutes | What it builds), a checklist of cheap tools worth trying (pencil grips, short crayons, slant board) and when not to bother, and a callout on when hand pain needs a professional look.

tools.title: Practice plan
tools.subtitle: 5 minutes a day, 2 weeks
tools.prompt: Build a 2-week, 5-minute daily practice plan for '{goal}' for the profile child, style and stage. Sections: a table (Day | Warm-up | Focus letters or shapes | Fun application e.g. label a drawing, write a joke), bullets on keeping it playful, a checklist of what 'done' looks like at the end of week 2, and a callout on stopping when frustration rises.

tools.title: Ready to write?
tools.subtitle: Pre-writing readiness check
tools.prompt: Create a 10-minute play-based pre-writing readiness check for the profile child's age and stage. Sections: a table of 8 tasks (Task | Materials | Expected for age | Watch for), a checklist to tick during play, bullets on what patterns of results suggest, and a callout on when to focus on play and fine-motor strength rather than letters.

disclaimer: General handwriting guidance, not an occupational-therapy assessment. See a GP, paediatrician or OT about persistent pain, a very weak grip or motor concerns.
